title: Consolidated Inference API PRD and Launch Playbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description: PRD for a single, unified hosted inference API surface that supports chat, completions, embeddings, and reranking with a shared auth/quotas model and clear compatibility guarantees for existing customers. This document defines functional requirements, acceptance criteria, constrained scope for launch, open trade-offs, rollout and monitoring plans, and a launch checklist with post-launch follow-ups.
background_and_rationale: Customers currently use separate legacy endpoints with divergent request/response shapes and billing semantics; this causes integration friction and makes SDK support and observability inconsistent.

Goal: provide a converged, developer-friendly API that reduces cognitive load, consolidates telemetry/quotas, and enables feature parity (streaming, tool-calls, structured outputs) while preserving backwards compatibility for the 20 highest-volume customers.
Decision constraints: minimize breaking changes, keep per-token billing semantics aligned with existing hosted API, and ship with a clear deprecation path for legacy endpoints.
goals: GA: Unified API that can serve chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank workloads with single SDK and REST contract.
Performance: median tail latency <= existing hosted endpoints for 95% of production traffic under typical load patterns.
Reliability: rollout with canary, automatic fallback to compatible model variants, and SLOs defined for critical routes.
Developer ergonomics: streaming responses, structured output JSON mode, and tool/function-calling primitives supported at launch.
scope_included: API surface: /v1/inference endpoint with intent parameter (chat|completions|embeddings|rerank)
Streaming: server-sent event (SSE) streaming to match existing streaming semantics for chat and completions.
Billing: single per-token billing meter; embed unit conversion for embedding calls documented.
Compatibility: backwards-compatible request mapping layer for 4 top legacy endpoints during rollout window.
Console: per-route observability dashboards and token-level cost breakdown for the new routes at GA.
Security: KMS integration for Private customers and mandatory TLS; enterprise SSO mapping for caller identity.
scope_out_of_scope: On-prem packaged installer for Private (will remain on Private roadmap; not in this hosted launch).
New model catalog onboarding (catalog updates continue on normal cadence).
Advanced autoscaling policies for Dedicated; dedicated autoscaling work remains in Dedicated roadmap.
requirements: Request contract must support: input prompt(s), optional system messages, tool call hints, user metadata (opaque map), streaming flag, model hint, temperature/top_p, max_tokens, and response format (text|json-schema).
Responses must include stable identifiers for tokens and structured metadata (model_id, model_version, latency_ms, billing_tokens).
Embeddings route must accept single or batched inputs and return consistent vector dimensionality matching model specs.
Rerank must accept candidate list <= 1000 with stable scoring output and deterministic tie-break behavior documented.
SDKs (JS + Python) must expose unified client and preserve existing helper functions for streaming and function-calling.
Telemetry must emit request_id, route, model, request_size_tokens, response_size_tokens, start_time, end_time, and worker_region for every request.
nonfunctional_requirements: Latency: p50/p95/p99 targets defined per route; p95 for chat/completions <= 350ms on small models for 1-2 token responses under steady state in hosted fleet.
Throughput: support sustained 10k RPS for lightweight embedding batch sizes across multi-region footprint with graceful degradation.
SLOs: 99.9% availability for API control plane; 99% for streaming connections over 30-day window.
Cost: per-token cost should not increase >5% for customers after migration; Optimize team to provide quantization suggestions to keep costs neutral.
acceptance_criteria: Contract: API passes contract conformance test-suite (server + SDK) with 100% of golden examples for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank.
Backward compatibility: adapter layer correctly proxies 95% of recorded legacy traffic patterns with no functional regressions in first canary wave.
Performance: automated load tests demonstrate p95 latency <= defined thresholds for selected model profiles; cost per request measured and within expected bounds.
Security: security review completed and security_review_required checklist items signed off by Security team.
Observability: dashboards show token-level cost breakdown and tracing hooks are wired to per-request trace IDs.
SDKs: JS and Python GA SDKs released and dependabot-enabled with example migration guide in docs.
acceptance_test_plan: Unit + integration test suites added to monorepo: contract tests for request/response shapes.
Synthetic canary: run 48-hour canary against 10% of traffic with rollback automation if error rate > 1% or latency > 2x baseline.
Customer beta: onboard 3 strategic customers to opt-in migration and capture migration feedback within first 2 weeks.
Chaos tests: induce KV cache misses and node preemption to validate fallback paths.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Internal): API available to internal teams and feature flags enabled for self-serve testing (2 weeks).
Phase 1 (Canary): Route 5-10% low-risk traffic; monitor key metrics; automatic rollback triggers configured (1 week).
Phase 2 (Gradual Ramp): 50% traffic split and opt-in migration window for high-volume accounts (2 weeks).
Phase 3 (GA): full migration, deprecate legacy endpoints with 90-day notice and migration docs (post-GA).
launch_checklist: API docs published with migration guide and example snippets for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank.
JS and Python SDKs released and published to npm/pypi with migration examples and changelogs.
Console dashboards created: per-route latency, errors, token cost, rollout progress, and active model versions.
Canary automation: rollout job + automatic rollback configured in infra with on-call paging rules.
Security signoff: threat model review, pen-test items tracked and closed or accepted with mitigations.
Legal/compliance: Terms update and data residency mapping completed for EU/UK regions.
Support: runbook created, triage flow defined, and postmortem template prepared.
Billing: conversion table for embedding units and billing rendered in Console and invoices.
Communication: customer announcement draft, migration webinars scheduled, and status page templates ready.
monitoring_and_slos: Health checks for control-plane endpoints and streaming connectivity with 15s heartbeat.
Per-route SLO dashboards: availability, error budget burn rate, latency percentiles.
Alerting thresholds: error_rate > 0.5% sustained 10m => P1; p95 latency > 2x baseline => P1.
Synthetic probes: cross-region real-user simulation every 5m to detect regression in latency or ordering.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Breaking integrations for legacy customers. Mitigation: maintain adapter compatibility layer and offer dedicated migration support for top 20 customers.
Risk: Increased cost for high-embedding-volume customers. Mitigation: Optimize team to provide quantization/packing suggestions and temporary credits for early movers.
Risk: Streaming connection instability at scale. Mitigation: phased canary, increased connection pool limits, and backoff recommendations in SDKs.
open_questions_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: unified billing model simplifies UX but obscures historical per-endpoint metrics for some customers; decided to keep per-route cost breakdown in Console.
Question: Should rerank support >1000 candidates at GA? Decision: cap at 1000 and schedule higher-limit support in a follow-up riff.
Tradeoff: Default structured JSON output vs free-form text — we will require explicit response_format=json-schema for structured output to avoid regressions.
security_and_privacy_notes: All hosted requests are logged for billing and telemetry; PII redaction rules applied by default with opt-out for Private customers.
KMS integration must be validated for token encryption at rest for enterprise tenants; Security team to provide checklist.
post_launch_followups: Migration analytics: measure % of customers migrated after 30/60/90 days and identify friction points.
Retention: collect and prioritize SDK/API feedback and ship iterative fixes in first 8 weeks.
Deprecated endpoints: publish deprecation timeline and automated redirector for legacy SDKs.
